scope: 66 remaining-batch source-bound UIDs plus current post-D q26 input
activeTemplateSearchReason: The supplied ACTIVE templates were reviewed for polynomial division and remainder methods. Related factor, divisibility, limit, and derivative templates do not match these procedures exactly; no ACTIVE template key is assigned.

clusters.label: Linear-divisor root evaluation
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Evaluate the dividend at a monic linear divisor root to obtain its constant remainder; if it is zero, use exact factorization to evaluate the quotient, and for integer residues verify the standard range.
clusters.mergeRationale: These items use the same root-value remainder transfer. Shared roots of composite divisors, quotient follow-up after zero remainder, and numeric range checks are applications of that one step.

clusters.label: Low-degree value interpolation
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Represent the relevant low-degree polynomial or remainder, transfer values from distinct divisor roots, solve the resulting coefficient equations, then evaluate the requested value.
clusters.mergeRationale: Each item reconstructs coefficients from polynomial values at linear roots; values may come from a supplied remainder, exact divisibility, or a prior division identity.

clusters.label: Composite-remainder extension
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Combine remainder information on factor divisors by writing the dividend as a base or common remainder plus a multiple of the known factor product; use additional root/value constraints to determine the correction.
clusters.mergeRationale: These items extend a remainder across added linear factors or use equal remainders across several divisors; the added values fix the remaining terms.

clusters.label: Evaluate a supplied division identity
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Substitute the requested input into a supplied dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder identity; use another input if needed to recover a quotient value.
clusters.mergeRationale: The quotient and remainder are supplied; evaluating the same identity provides the requested dividend or quotient values.

clusters.label: Linked division identities
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Write the quotient-remainder identities for the same polynomial, exploit shared or constrained quotient/remainder terms and degree bounds, then solve consistency conditions.
clusters.mergeRationale: These methods depend on compatibility among successive or parallel divisions, including common intermediates, equal terms, and degree restrictions.

clusters.label: Synthetic-division recurrence
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Apply the synthetic-division multiply-add recurrence at the linear divisor root; read quotient coefficients and final remainder, rescaling the quotient for a nonmonic divisor.
clusters.mergeRationale: All rows use the same recurrence; a missing table cell or nonmonic divisor changes presentation/scaling, not the solution pattern.

clusters.label: Long-division leading-term cancellation
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Cancel the current leading term with a divisor multiple, update the residual, and continue until residual degree is below divisor degree.
clusters.mergeRationale: The text and pictured long-division layouts express the same iterative algorithm; display format is not a separate L4 type.

clusters.label: Factor-theorem root constraints
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Translate stated linear factors or divisibility into zero evaluations at their roots, then solve or test coefficients and residual factors; branch when a product of values is zero.
clusters.mergeRationale: These items use root vanishing to establish factors or reject candidates, including product-zero branches and common-factor checks.

clusters.label: Repeated linear-factor multiplicity
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: For a squared linear factor, require the dividend to vanish at the root and then require the first quotient to vanish at the same root.
clusters.mergeRationale: All items enforce multiplicity two through successive factor-theorem conditions on the dividend and quotient.

clusters.label: Assign named monic factors after coefficient recovery
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Use a prescribed factor root to determine the polynomial, factor out known roots, then use degree, irreducibility, monicity, or a relation between residual factors to assign them and check uniqueness.
clusters.mergeRationale: Both items first constrain roots and then assign labeled factors from the residual factorization; one remains HOLD because its stated normalization is insufficient.

clusters.label: Shifted-basis identity coefficients
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: For an identity in powers of x−r, apply synthetic division repeatedly at r to extract coefficients from constant term upward.
clusters.mergeRationale: Both identities use repeated coefficient extraction in a translated polynomial basis; centers and requested coefficient expressions do not create separate types.

clusters.label: Global identity special-value reduction
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Use a special input in a global polynomial identity to force a structural relation, then combine the resulting polynomial expressions and evaluate the requested value or remainder.
clusters.mergeRationale: One uses a sum-of-squares zero and the other sum/difference identities; both reduce global identities at decisive inputs to reconstruct polynomial values.

clusters.label: High-power modular reduction
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Derive a short power-cycle congruence from the divisor, reduce high exponents modulo that cycle, collect terms, and normalize below the divisor degree.
clusters.mergeRationale: This is a distinct modular-reduction route; no separate skeleton is made for individual exponents.

clusters.label: Transform a division identity under multiplication
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Multiply a known quotient-remainder identity and regroup terms by the new divisor to identify transformed quotient and lower-degree remainder.
clusters.mergeRationale: This is one transferable division-identity transformation.

clusters.label: Choose an extremal remainder candidate
clusters.canonicalSkeleton: Use a remainder condition at one linear divisor root to restrict a polynomial value, map the second divisor root to that input, then compare possible remainders.
clusters.mergeRationale: The linked root conditions yield two sign-related candidates and the minimum selects one; this is more than a fixed-value remainder lookup.

clusters.label: No separate L4 skeleton
clusters.mergeRationale: The supplied remainder polynomial is read directly and two terms are added; a new skeleton would only encode a one-step coefficient read.
